title: Jama Masjid Street Food Delhi - Best Mughlai Dishes & Famous Restaurants
content:
Jama Masjid Street Food - Delhi,

When it comes to food in Delhi, nothing beats the charm of Jama Masjid Street Food. Located in the heart of Old Delhi, this bustling food lane is heaven for food lovers who crave authentic Mughlai flavors, kebabs, biryanis, and traditional sweets. The aroma of grilled meat, sizzling tandoors, and freshly prepared delicacies makes this street one of the most famous food hubs in Delhi.

The area around Jama Masjid has been a food hub since the Mughal era. With the Jama Masjid mosque being one of Shah Jahan’s grand creations, the surrounding streets naturally grew into a marketplace catering to worshippers and visitors. Over time, it became home to some of Delhi’s oldest and most iconic eateries, many of which still preserve age-old Mughlai recipes.

What Makes Jama Masjid Street Food Special?

  • Authentic Mughlai Flavors – From kebabs to biryani, the food here takes you back to the royal Mughal kitchens.
  • Historic Eateries – Many food shops here are over 50–100 years old.
  • Budget-Friendly Feast – You can try a variety of dishes without spending much.
  • Late-Night Food Hub – Many stalls and shops stay open late, perfect for food walks.
  • Blend of Culture & Taste – Experience Delhi’s rich history while enjoying its most famous food.

Famous Food to Try:

Here’s what you must eat at Jama Masjid street food lane:

  • Kebabs at Karim’s & Al Jawahar – Iconic spots for melt-in-mouth seekh kebabs, mutton kebabs, and chicken tikka.
  • Biryani – Flavorful Mughlai biryani cooked in traditional dum style.
  • Butter Chicken – Rich and creamy, a must-try dish at Al Jawahar.
  • Changezi Chicken – A Mughal-era dish full of spices and flavors.
  • Mutton Nihari – Slow-cooked overnight, best enjoyed in the morning.
  • Kheer, Phirni & Shahi Tukda – Traditional desserts that perfectly end the food walk.
  • Cool Drinks & Sharbats – Try refreshing lassi and flavored sharbats after the spicy food.

How to Reach:

  • Nearest Metro Station: Jama Masjid Metro (Violet Line), or Chawri Bazar Metro (Yellow Line).
  • By Auto/Taxi: Easily accessible from anywhere in Delhi.
  • Parking Information: Limited parking around Jama Masjid, best to use metro or rickshaw.

Famous Restaurants & Food Joints Near Jama Masjid:

  • Karim’s – Iconic 100-year-old eatery famous worldwide.
  • Al Jawahar – Known for butter chicken, biryani, and Mughlai curries.
  • Aslam Chicken Corner – Famous for buttery grilled chicken.
  • Cool Point – Must-try shahi tukda and kheer.
  • Haji Shabrati Nihariwale – For early morning nihari lovers.

Nearby Attractions:

After a food walk, you can also visit:

  • Jama Masjid – One of India’s largest mosques.
  • Red Fort – UNESCO World Heritage Site nearby.
  • Chandni Chowk Market – Famous for shopping and street food.
excerpt: Jama Masjid Street Food is more than just a food lane – it’s an experience of Delhi’s history, culture, and flavors. From the world-famous Karim’s kebabs to buttery chicken at Al Jawahar, refreshing sharbats, and rich Mughlai desserts, every bite tells a story of Old Delhi’s heritage. Whether you’re a foodie, traveler, or just curious to explore, a walk through these lanes is a must-have food journey in Delhi.
